Chapter Four: Challenging the Rules of Gender and Power
You ever notice how the rules about who gets to speak, who gets to lead, and who really gets taken seriously… well, they’re everywhere? You see them in boardrooms, in classrooms, even in the stories we’re told on TV and in movies.
And for anyone who doesn’t quite fit the mold, that path to power? It's absolutely packed with obstacles—some are right out in the open, but a lot of them are hidden, almost invisible.
Growing up, the lessons about gender weren’t always loud, but wow, were they persistent. Girls were supposed to be agreeable, look after everyone else, and definitely not make waves. Ambition? Oh, that was great in boys… but in girls? Suddenly, it was called arrogance. The world seemed to reward those who played along and punish anyone who dared to push back, especially if you were expected to just stay quiet.
As we got older, those double standards became impossible to ignore. Everywhere—in the workplace, in relationships, out in public—you could see it play out over and over. If a woman spoke her mind, she was labeled as difficult. But a man doing the same thing? He was seen as confident. The exact same behavior, but two totally different reactions. Sound familiar?
Then, there’s that moment—maybe you’ve had it—when after one too many meetings where your ideas are ignored until someone else repeats them, you just decide: enough. No more waiting for permission. That’s when it hits you—the rules aren’t set in stone. They’re just old habits, kept alive by repetition and, honestly, by fear. So, speaking up, claiming your ideas, demanding respect—it feels risky. But the alternative, staying silent, starts to feel impossible.
Of course, there’s backlash. People say you’re being too sensitive, too aggressive, just… too much. Even friends and coworkers, maybe without realizing it, suggest you tone it down, pick your battles, or try to be a bit more “likable.” But the more you push back, the clearer it becomes—the real problem isn’t your attitude. It’s the system that penalizes women for standing up for themselves.
So, here’s something to really pay attention to: fighting for gender equality isn’t just about laws or policies. It’s about changing how people think, the stories they share, even the jokes they laugh at. It’s about challenging the belief that power only belongs to a select few.
Think about popular culture for a second. The characters we see on TV, the heroes in movies, even the headlines we read—they all reinforce this idea that only certain people should lead, and the rest should follow. If we want to change the culture, we have to change those stories. That means inviting in new voices, fresh perspectives, and a willingness to get loud, even when it feels uncomfortable.
Most folks have no idea how much energy it takes just to navigate these unwritten rules. Deciding to break them? That’s not just about personal ambition. It’s about making space for others to do the same. Every time you refuse to be quiet, every act of defiance—it chips away at the old structures that keep power locked up tight.
And you know what helps? Humor. Finding ways to joke about how absurd these rules can be, pointing out the contradictions and double standards—it makes the journey a little lighter. Sometimes, laughter is the best protest. It highlights the flaws in the system, and keeps hope alive.
The road to equality is long, and, let’s face it, it can be pretty frustrating. But for anyone who’s spent a lifetime being told to be quiet, just speaking up is a win. It’s proof that the rules really can change, that power is something we can share, and that everyone—absolutely everyone—deserves to be heard.
